text:
Alex M: FYI saw weird tail-latency spikes on the partner bench when we pushed kernel patch v3.2.1 — looks correlated with sustained perf/W runs above 65C.
Samir: ugh. which bench? the 4xA100 node at partner lab?
Alex M: yep. partner reported CPU fan curves reactive, GPU temps crossing 72C after ~30m.
Jessie: can you paste the HWMON logs + the perf trace? even a 30s window around the spike helps.
Alex M: pasted below (snip):
```
[2026-03-20T14:03:12Z] throughput=480tps power=725W gpu0_temp=71C gpu1_temp=73C tail_p99=240ms
[2026-03-20T14:03:44Z] throughput=485tps power=730W gpu0_temp=73C gpu1_temp=75C tail_p99=560ms
```
Samir: looks like a thermal-throttle/clock-droop event rather than model issue. did kernel revert to safe DVFS? need dmesg around that time.
Priya: partner said they applied our kernel tunables (sched/irq affinity) + our Raven kernel blob. Did they also enable the new powercap driver? (@Samir)
Samir: not sure. pinged partner infra team for confirmation.
bench-bot: scheduled bench run #442: model=redwood-rlhf-small seq=2048 duration=45m target=480tps
Jessie: actionable plan: 1) reproduce in-house on identical board, 2) enable continuous hw telemetry streaming to S3, 3) run with and without our kernel patch to isolate. Who can spin the node?
Alex M: I'll book a slot on the local bench tomorrow morning. need a short test script — here's what I run:
```
./run_perf.sh --model redwood-rlhf-small --seq 2048 --duration 00:45:00 --target-tps 480 --telemetry enabled
```
Priya: add `--hwmon-interval 1s` and `--collect-dmesg` so we catch fast events.
Alex M: done.
Samir: if it reproduces, we'll try toggling powercap: `echo 0 > /sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:0/enabled` (partner might need admin). We should also run a short kernel with debug clocks enabled.
Jessie: also want a heatmap of perf/W vs clock bins. can we log per-core clocks every 5s and aggregate?
bench-bot: telemetry upload for run #442 completed: s3://redwood-bench/partner-lab/2026-03-20/run442/ (logs + perf traces)
Alex M: grabbing logs now. @Samir @Jessie I'll paste dmesg section if I find throttling messages.
Samir: ping partner infra for fan-curve config and BMC sensor offsets. sometimes OEM fudges calibration.
Priya: ETA from partner infra? we need to know if this is lab-only or field risk before the marketplace announcement.
PartnerInfra (via email): "We see the same spikes; fans ramped late due to conservative BMC thresholds. We're pushing updated fan-curve to the rack and will re-run tests tonight." (cc @Priya)
Jessie: good. once they re-run, ask them to capture 5-minute preheat baseline + the 45m run. we want perf/W delta vs baseline.
Alex M: next steps on our side: reproduce locally, attempt with powercap off, and run kernel-with-debug. I'll log artifacts to the shared folder and ping for a quick sync.
Samir: if we confirm kernel interaction, we should prepare a short joint note (private) to partner engineering with repro steps and recommended defaults (fan curve, powercap, DVFS knobs).
Priya: agree. also flag product/marketplace that launch comms should skip hardware-specific perf claims until resolved.
Jessie: I'll draft the partner engineering note and include a heatmap template and the small repro script.
Alex M: thanks. I'll update this thread after the local run (~tomorrow 09:00 PST).
Priya: :thumbsup:
Alex M: local run reproduced the spike. attaching dmesg snippet: `thermal_throttle: GPU0 clock drop from 1530MHz -> 810MHz at temp 74C`
Samir: ok that's actionable. schedule kernel bisect with the partner this week. tagging @bench-bot to queue a bisect run.
bench-bot: bisect job queued: job_id=bisect-77 target=partner-lab node=4xA100 expected-duration=6h
Jessie: thanks everyone. once bisect narrows to patch set, we'll coordinate a short eng-to-eng call.
Alex M: leaving here — will post bisect results when available.
